1030.author: zhaozhaozz
1030.body:
The Docker image job failed in the merge queue because the pinned micromamba download from GitHub releases returned `504` three times in a row. `scripts/fetch-managed-micromamba.mjs` gave up after about six seconds: three attempts, two and four seconds apart. GitHub release downloads fail in bursts that last longer than that, and the Docker job builds cold on purpose (its comment explains why it is uncached), so it has no cache to fall back on. The same downloader runs for every `docker compose build`.

## Back off for about a minute

`downloadBytesWithRetry` now makes up to six attempts with exponential backoff: 2, 4, 8, 16 and 30 seconds between them, about a minute in all, with each delay capped at 30 seconds. Which failures are retried is unchanged: 408, 429, 5xx, network errors and timeouts are; a 404 or a checksum mismatch still fails at once. The log line names the next delay.

No cache was added. The Docker job's cold build is deliberate, and the downloader's existing `BINARY_CACHE_DIR` / `BINARY_CACHE_URL` / conda mirror options remain the way to avoid the network when that is wanted.

## Validation

- `node --test scripts/binary-release/fetch-managed-micromamba.test.mjs`: 11 tests, 11 passed. One new test returns `504` five times and asserts the delays `[2000, 4000, 8000, 16000, 30000]` and the sixth-attempt success. It then asserts that six consecutive `504`s give up with the `504` error after five waits. The wait is injected, so the test does not sleep.
- `node --test scripts/binary-release/*.test.mjs`: 33 tests, 32 passed. The one failure, `runner-sea.test.mjs`, imports `packages/executor/dist/runner-bundle.js`, which this unbuilt worktree does not have; the test does not touch the downloader.
- The Docker image was not rebuilt locally. The change is confined to the retry loop, which the tests above exercise.

## E2E user journeys

Not applicable: no product, API, CLI or Runner behaviour changes. The only path affected is building the image, and it changes only how long a transient download failure is retried.

## Release
Release category: release:fix
User impact: `docker compose build` and the Docker CI job ride out about a minute of micromamba download errors (502/503/504, 429, timeouts) instead of failing after about six seconds.
Compatibility and migration: none.
1030.head: fix/micromamba-download-retries
1030.title: fix(build): retry the micromamba download through a minute of release outage

1031.author: zhaozhaozz
1031.body:
Closing the API closed the store's database but did not wait for the store's file writes. State arrays (`session-runs`, and the like), run stream appends, subagent mutations and workspace-file mutations each run on a per-path queue (`mkdir`, temporary file, rename). A write queued by a run or probe that ended during shutdown kept going after `closeApiServer` resolved. On SIGTERM the process exits right after `closeApiServer`, which can cut such a write off. In tests, the fixture removes the data directory while the write is still in flight.

That race failed four merge queue UT runs on 2026-11-09, each time in a different `services/api/src/server.test.ts` case: `desktop skill switches…`, `global Runner management routes…`, `updating SSH credentials immediately probes…` and `request errors after headers…`. The worker events show the two forms. In three runs, a pending `mkdir` recreated a directory being removed: `ENOTEMPTY: directory not empty, rmdir` in the after hook. In the other, a pending `session-runs` state rename found its directory gone: `ENOENT … rename …/session-runs/.state-…`.

## The API waits for queued writes before closing the store

`SessionStore.whenWritesSettle()` awaits every entry of the store's write queues and the catalog save queue, then checks again, because a write that settles can queue another. The re-check is bounded at 100 passes, so a writer that keeps re-queuing cannot hold shutdown forever. The API lifecycle awaits it as the last cleanup step, immediately before `store.close()`. The SIGTERM path keeps its existing 15-second limit.

## Test fixtures remove data directories with retries

Writes the store does not own (a probe, a sidecar) can still land after close. `removeTestRoot` already retried for that reason (`maxRetries: 10`). Six `server.test.ts` fixtures removed their directory with a plain `rm`, including three of the four that failed. They now use the same options, defined once as `retryingRemoval`.

## Validation

- New `store.test.ts` case: a state write blocked on a gate, which queues a second write when it finishes. `whenWritesSettle()` does not resolve while the gate is closed; after release, both files hold their values and no temporary file is left. As a reverse check, a `whenWritesSettle()` that returns immediately makes this case fail.
- `node --import tsx --test src/server.test.ts`: 112 tests, 110 passed, 2 failed. Both failures are pre-existing in this environment and fail identically on unmodified `main` files: the PDF upload case needs `services/paper/.venv`, and `API runs one observable subagent through task and keeps nested task denied` fails its assertion on `main` as well.
- `node --import tsx --test "src/**/*.test.ts"` in `services/api`: 2044 tests, 2033 passed, 11 failed, 0 cancelled. All 11 fail the same way with this change's three source files restored to `main`, or fail on missing local prerequisites: five need Python virtualenvs this worktree does not have (`services/paper/.venv` for three PDF cases, `services/evolve/.venv` for the IdeaTree and evolve-thinking journeys); five are `specialist-runtime/process-adapters.st.test.ts` Claude/ACP transport cases, which also fail on `main` here; one is the subagent case above. None involves shutdown or data-directory removal.
- `pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/api typecheck` and `tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json`: no errors.

## E2E user journeys

Not run. No request, response or UI behaviour changes: the change orders shutdown steps (queued writes before the store closes) and is covered by the store test above and by every API test that closes a server. A user-visible journey would need a SIGTERM delivered while a write is queued, which the existing E2E layers do not drive. This is a coverage gap, not a pass.

## Release
Release category: release:fix
User impact: stopping the API (SIGTERM) no longer exits while queued run-state or stream writes are still being written; flaky `server.test.ts` failures in UT stop.
Compatibility and migration: none. Shutdown can take as long as the queued writes, within the existing 15-second SIGTERM limit.
1031.head: fix/api-close-settles-store-writes
1031.title: fix(api): let queued store writes land before the API closes its store

1032.author: moShangLouTou
1032.body:
Desktop now opens model setup whenever the model catalog is empty, including after the last model is removed. New sessions and the first session of a new project automatically select a configured model so users can start without an additional selection step when the global task model is unset.

Model selection follows explicit user choice, project default, global task model, then the first model in the catalog's existing name order. A fallback is saved only on the new session and survives reloads and catalog reordering. Existing defaults, historical sessions, and recovery for explicitly selected deleted models retain their behavior.

## Validation

Rebased onto upstream `main` at `c3678320acb2ce31fc5390c640a1f6bf5e9f6bcd` without conflicts. Verified on head `c8ef27a10fd28835cb1c7ca817467d6a7b996367`, locally by Codex on Linux x64 with Node 22.19.0:

- Desktop bootstrap, model setup, and model refresh tests: **16 passed, 0 failed/skipped**.
- API model selection tests: **17 passed, 0 failed/skipped**, loading workspace sources through a temporary tsx path map.
- Desktop and API typechecks, the targeted API test typecheck, and `git diff --check upstream/main`: passed.

Full local suites, browser/E2E journeys, and native Windows/macOS validation were not run. Manual product verification remains for empty-catalog startup, removing the last model, completing setup, and creating sessions/projects with no global task model.

Release category: `release:fix`.
